lockup.summary: The company, its directors, its officers and holders of 5% or more have agreed not to sell shares for 180 days. For the company, this runs from the closing of the offering. For insiders, it runs from the date the prospectus takes effect.

what: It provides employer-of-record, HR outsourcing, executive search and HR research services to clients in Hong Kong, through its subsidiary TalentQuest.
proceeds: It expects net proceeds of about US$26.2 million. About 30% is for growth in the Asia Pacific market, 30% for adding artificial intelligence to the business, and 40% for general costs and working capital.
risks: The Chinese government could step in or change the rules at any time, which could hurt the Hong Kong business and make the shares lose value.
Following Hong Kong's personal data privacy law and similar rules may cost a lot and could hurt the business.
The Hong Kong National Security Law could affect its Hong Kong subsidiary, which makes up almost all of its business.
There are political risks in doing business in Hong Kong.
It earns money in Hong Kong dollars but the shares trade in US dollars, so currency changes could affect your investment value.
